- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overreacts with continued upward trend; cap forecast growth to 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day to reflect mean reversion.
- Model frequently fails to capture early mean reversion after high volatility; if 3–5 days of high sentiment followed by low sentiment, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price volatility; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
